cluster_summary: This cluster covers multiple vulnerabilities in XWiki where dynamic code execution (especially Velocity templates) is performed without proper authorization checks, input validation, or sandbox restrictions. The issues include missing script/programming rights checks, insufficient method-level sandboxing, validation gaps for document origins, and incorrect handling of default content types. Fixes involve adding authorization checks, method whitelists, and proper default values to prevent unauthorized code execution.
guideline_text: Trace lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities into server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs. Report code paths where a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 11 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege.

mechanism.missing_guard: a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability
mechanism.name: privileged server-side capability exposed to lower privilege context
mechanism.sink_shape: server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs
mechanism.source_shape: lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities
mechanism.typical_fix: check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Deprecate the method and add a programming rights check before execution.
sub_patterns.name: Missing authorization on public API method
sub_patterns.root_cause: The public API method `invokeServletAndReturnAsString` was exposed without an authorization check, allowing users with SCRIPT right to read arbitrary files.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add a per-class method whitelist (Map<Class, Set<String>>) and check lowercased method names before allowing execution.
sub_patterns.name: Insufficient method-level sandbox restrictions
sub_patterns.root_cause: The Velocity sandbox only restricted which classes could be used, not which methods could be called on allowed classes like java.io.File, allowing arbitrary method invocation.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add validation using XARExtensionIndex.isExtensionDocument() to ensure the document is from an installed extension before allowing execution.
sub_patterns.name: Missing validation of document origin for dynamic code execution
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code assumed any document could be executed as a script without checking if it belongs to an installed XAR extension.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Pass the document object (DocumentModelBridge) directly to the evaluation function to ensure consistent authorization context.
sub_patterns.name: Authorization context mismatch during Velocity evaluation
sub_patterns.root_cause: Authorization was checked on a document object but the execution context used a reference that could resolve to a different document, leading to privilege escalation.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add authorization checks (e.g., using AuthorExecutor or direct rights check) before allowing Velocity evaluation, ensuring only authorized users can execute code.
sub_patterns.name: Missing authorization before Velocity code execution from user-controlled content
sub_patterns.root_cause: Velocity templates or code from user-controlled sources (UI extensions, document properties, skin files, configurable class properties) were executed without verifying the user has the required script right or appropriate authorization.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Default null content type to WIKI_TEXT and ensure the analysis runs for that case; restructure switch to include a default case.
sub_patterns.name: Missing default content type handling in rights analysis
sub_patterns.root_cause: The rights analysis function assumed the content type of a TextArea property is always non-null, skipping analysis when null and allowing unvalidated macros to execute.
